evidence.label: Regional GRACE and Kansas well observations
evidence.text:
Regional water storage & nearby Kansas wells

GRACE measures total terrestrial water storage across a broad region, not an individual aquifer, well or field. Groundwater, soil moisture, surface water and snow can contribute. These observations do not change crop rankings or Field Watch status.

Regional-only total terrestrial water storage versus separate point well observations. Not a field/well forecast, pumping measurement or irrigation allocation.

NASA/JPL GRACE/GRACE-FO RL06.3Mv04 CRI · mascon 861 · ~3-degree equal-area mascon; 0.5-degree display grid is NOT independent field-scale resolution. Native grid-cell center 38.25, -100.75 identifies a regional estimate, not the selected field.

2004–2009 time-mean baseline (2004.000 to 2009.999); cm equivalent water thickness anomaly. Display period January 2015–December 2025. 21 missing months, including the inter-mission gap, remain gaps. Source coverage 2002-04-16T00:00:00Z to 2026-09-16T23:59:59Z. Retrieved 2026-11-15T13:29:00.029550+00:00.

Representative grid cell in the actual native mascon_ID containing Finney demo; unscaled CRI lwe_thickness, no gain factors, no added GAD, no groundwater subtraction, no smoothing or rebaselining. Uncertainty is native mascon 1-sigma, not independent pixel errors.

Scale and interpretation limitation. Direction agreement is descriptive, not validation: total terrestrial storage includes groundwater, soil moisture, surface water and snow. Nearby wells do not validate a broad mascon or predict this field’s own well.

Matched-period trend comparison and dated well records
Monthly regional storage, uncertainty and gaps

NASA/JPL / PO.DAAC product and citation · DOI 10.5067/TEMSC-3JC634. NASA/JPL, NASA/DLR GRACE and NASA/GFZ GRACE-FO; PO.DAAC.

Kansas Geological Survey WIZARD · KGS disclaimer. Local observations are not definitive validation of a mascon. No prediction of the farmer’s own well, pumping or allocation follows.

run.rule: Dry spell: rain in the last 14 days and root-zone soil wetness are both at or below the 20th percentile for this time of year. Watch: either one is at or below the 30th percentile. Without soil data, low rain gives at most Watch. Cut-offs follow the U.S. Drought Monitor's percentile bands (D0 = 21st–30th, D1 = 11th–20th); they are demonstration settings, not agronomic standards. Water balance and the Kansas drought outlook are shown as context and do not change the status. Rule version 2.
